lessons.title: 1. What are people actually trading?
lessons.takeaway: A financial trade exchanges money, a financial item or promises about future payments.

sections.title: The idea
paragraphs: You buy a used bicycle for $100. You exchange cash for an item. Tomorrow someone offers $110 for it. The purchase price is still $100, but its possible selling value has changed. This is only an analogy for cost versus current value; bicycles are not financial instruments.

A share is a small ownership interest in a company. A bond is different: it is a borrowing arrangement, usually with interest payments and a promised repayment. A derivative is a contract whose value depends on something else, such as an interest rate, exchange rate or share price. You will meet swaps and options later; you do not need their pricing formulas yet.

A trade records an agreement: who buys or sells, which instrument, how much, at what price, in what currency and when. The other party is the counterparty. Settlement is when the agreed payment and delivery are completed. Agreement and settlement need not happen on the same day.
A bank may trade to meet a customer's need, manage an existing exposure or pursue an investment/trading strategy. The purpose does not remove the need to record and value the contract correctly.

sections.title: A concrete example
sections.example:
A fictional bank buys 10 shares of Company A from Dealer B at $100 per share.
Instrument: Company A shares
Counterparty: Dealer B
Quantity: 10 shares
Agreed price: $100 per share
Cash price before fees: 10 × $100 = $1,000

sections.title: Connect it to work
paragraphs: A trade row is a record of the agreement. The counterparty is not automatically the issuer: Company A issued the shares, but Dealer B sold them in this example.

quiz.question: In this example, what is the trade?
options: The agreement to buy 10 shares at $100 each
Every share the bank owns in every company
quiz.explanation: The trade is the specific agreement. The bank's combined holdings and profit are separate concepts.

lessons.title: 2. A trade is an event; a position is what remains
lessons.takeaway: Several trade events can build one position. Position quantity and position value are different numbers.

sections.title: The idea
paragraphs: Imagine a shopping history and the contents of your cupboard. The history lists events; the cupboard shows what remains. In the same way, a trade log lists purchases and sales, while a position records the holding or exposure at a specified time.

Continue with the bank's 10 shares. It buys another 5 of the same shares, then sells 4. Ignoring other changes, the resulting position is 10 + 5 − 4 = 11 shares. There are three trades and one combined position in this example.

If each share is now worth $102, the position value is 11 × $102 = $1,122. Eleven is a quantity; 102 is a price per share; 1,122 is a currency amount. Always keep the units attached. Derivatives need different valuation methods: their notional is not automatically their market value.

A positive holding is a simple long position. An opposite exposure is short. A price increase generally helps the long and hurts the short in these simple linear examples. Actual short selling may involve borrowing and delivery obligations; we introduce signed numbers before those mechanics.

sections.title: A concrete example
sections.example:
Trade 1: buy 10 shares
Trade 2: buy 5 shares
Trade 3: sell 4 shares
Position: +11 shares
Current price: $102 per share
Current value: $1,122

sections.title: Connect it to work
paragraphs: A position table is often derived from trade records, but real systems also need corporate actions, transfers, cancellations and settlement rules. Counting rows is not the same as summing quantities.

quiz.question: You buy 8 shares, buy 3 more and sell 2. What remains?
options: 3 shares because there were three trades
quiz.explanation: 8 + 3 − 2 = 9 shares. There are three events, but the resulting position is nine.

lessons.title: 3. Where do desks, books and portfolios fit?
lessons.takeaway: Books organise positions; desks organise people and trading activity. A book is not a product, a trade or a separate legal company.

sections.title: The idea
paragraphs: A large bank needs smaller groups to manage its activity. A desk is a team focused on particular trading work. It may manage several books. A book groups positions and their results. It does not refer to a notebook or necessarily to a bank account.

A legal entity is the company that legally holds the rights and obligations. A portfolio is a collection of positions considered together for some purpose. The same positions may be grouped differently for desk management, accounting, risk or regulatory reporting.

Our simplified map is: legal entity → desk → book → positions. Trade events feed those positions. Actual banks may use more levels or different relationships. In particular, "trading book versus banking book" is also regulatory language; it is not just the name of a trading desk's internal book.

Suppose one team has a customer-trading book and a hedge book. Moving a position between those books changes the grouping, but does not necessarily create a new transaction with an external party. A system must distinguish a book transfer from an external purchase.

sections.title: A concrete example
sections.example:
Fictional Bank Ltd, legal entity
  Equity trading desk, team
    Customer book, internal group
      Company A position: +11 shares
      Company C position: +20 shares
    Hedge book, another internal group

sections.title: Connect it to work
paragraphs: BookId, DeskId and LegalEntityId answer different questions. A mapping error can move the same value to the wrong report without changing the price at all.

quiz.question: A desk has two books containing positions in the same bond. Which statement is safest?
options: Each book must be a separate legal bank
The bond must have two different issuers
The books are groupings; check the entity and purpose separately
quiz.explanation: An internal grouping does not establish a separate legal entity or a different instrument.

lessons.title: 4. Price, value, cash and profit are not the same
lessons.takeaway: Buying, owning, valuing and selling are different events. A value can change before any cash is received.

sections.title: The idea
paragraphs: Use a fresh, simpler example: buy 10 shares at $100 each, for $1,000 before fees. Later the market price is $105. The holding is then worth $1,050. The $50 increase is an unrealised value gain while the holding remains open. Selling all 10 at $105 would produce $1,050 cash proceeds and a simple $50 realised gain before costs.

Cash proceeds are not the same as profit: the original $1,000 cost must be considered. Nor does a rise in estimated value mean cash has appeared in an account. The accounting treatment of gains depends on the instrument and framework; the arithmetic here isolates the basic idea.

An asset is a resource or right; a liability is an obligation. A derivative can have positive value for one party and negative value for the other. Not every contract is an asset for both sides. We use long-asset deductions in later labs and label that assumption.

Percent means "out of 100". A 5% change on $1,000 is $50. One basis point is 0.01 percentage point: a rate moving from 5.00% to 5.01% rises by 1 basis point. A bond quote of 98.50 per 100 of face means $985 for $1,000 face before accrued interest. It does not mean $98.50 for the whole bond holding.

sections.title: A concrete example
sections.example:
Quantity: 10 shares
Purchase price per share: $100
Purchase cost: $1,000
Current price per share: $105
Current value: $1,050
Simple unrealised gain: $50

sections.title: Connect it to work
paragraphs: P&L stands for profit and loss. Store quantity, price, value, cash flows and P&L in different fields. Never infer their units from the number alone.

quiz.question: You sell the 10 shares for $1,050 after paying $1,000. Before fees, the profit is…
quiz.explanation: Profit is $1,050 − $1,000 = $50. The $1,050 is sale proceeds, not profit.

lessons.title: 5. Who checks the bank's numbers?
lessons.takeaway: The team entering trades should not be the only team judging whether its values are supportable.

sections.title: The idea
paragraphs: The front office, often shortened to FO, is the trading or client-facing side of the bank. It records transactions and produces initial marks. A mark is the price or value being used today. The word does not tell you whether the number is independently supported.

Independent valuation control challenges the evidence behind those marks. Product control, finance, risk, operations and model-risk teams have related responsibilities. Names and boundaries differ by bank, so treat this as a functional map rather than a universal organisation chart.

IPV means Independent Price Verification. Ask: "Can an independent source support the price or model input?" A difference triggers investigation, not automatic proof that one side is wrong. Adjustments change a valuation for a defined reason. Fair Value Hierarchy describes the evidence behind the measurement. Prudent valuation examines uncertainty for regulatory capital.

These questions connect but are not interchangeable. A trade can pass an independent price comparison and still have an exit cost. It can have an uncertain input without a data-processing failure. A job completing successfully does not demonstrate that all records were included or correctly valued.

sections.title: A concrete example
sections.example:
Trader / front office: "Our mark is 100."
Independent check: "Comparable evidence says 99.8."
Investigation: "Are time, instrument and price basis aligned?"
Approved conclusion: correct, adjust, or retain with evidence.
Reporting: show the value, evidence and decisions separately.

quiz.question: What does a successful nightly valuation job prove by itself?
options: The job completed. Its business results still need checking
quiz.explanation: Technical success and business correctness are separate. Completeness, evidence and reconciliation controls are still needed.

lessons.title: 6. Read one trade record with confidence
lessons.takeaway: Read the row as a sentence before attempting its calculation.

sections.title: The idea
paragraphs: Read this fictional record aloud: "At this valuation date, Fictional Bank Ltd's equity desk has 10 Company A shares in its customer book, marked at $100 per share in USD." That sentence names the owner, group, instrument, quantity, price, currency and time.

Now ask what is missing. Where did the price come from? Is it a current observation? Are the shares the same class as the quoted instrument? Has the trade been cancelled? Does the position include all trades? A tidy row is not enough without those connections.
Read the explanation and worked example, then try the checkpoint. The glossary defines unfamiliar terms; the labs offer optional numerical practice.

You are ready to begin the main course when you can explain trade versus position, book versus desk, price versus value and value change versus cash. It is fine to revisit this introduction; the later lessons build on these distinctions.

lessons.title: 7. A bond is a timeline of payments
lessons.takeaway: Background for lesson 15 and lesson 17.

sections.title: Explanation
paragraphs: A cash flow is money paid or received at a particular time. A plain two-year bond with face value $1,000 and a 5% annual coupon promises $50 after year one and $1,050 after year two: the last coupon plus repayment. These are contractual promises, not guaranteed receipts if the issuer defaults.

Present value asks how much those future payments are worth today. In this simplified example, discount each payment at the same annual rate, then add the results. A market price can also reflect credit, liquidity and other effects; the flat-rate example isolates timing.

With the promised payments fixed, a higher discount rate makes each present value smaller. That is the basic reason an ordinary fixed-rate bond price tends to fall when required yields rise. It is not a universal direction rule for every security.

exercise.prompt: Try explaining: Why is the final cash flow $1,050 rather than $1,000?
exercise.solution: It contains both the final $50 coupon and the $1,000 principal repayment. Counting only principal omits a payment.

lessons.title: 8. Swaps and options: payment is not value
lessons.takeaway: Background for lesson 15, lesson 17 and lesson 21.

sections.title: Explanation
paragraphs: A fixed-for-floating interest-rate swap exchanges interest amounts. Assume a bank pays 4% fixed and receives a floating rate on $1m for a half-year period with accrual fraction 0.5. If the floating rate for that payment is 5%, it receives $25,000 and pays $20,000. If payment netting applies, the net receipt is $5,000. The $1m notional is only the reference amount in this example.

That one payment is not the entire swap value. Before settlement, value depends on all remaining expected net payments, their dates and discounting. A future floating payment may be unknown today, so a forecast curve is needed. A discount curve supplies discount factors. Different maturities can have different rates.

A call option gives its holder the right to buy an underlying asset at a strike price. With strike $100, its expiry payoff per share is max(share price − 100, 0). At expiry prices $90, $100 and $120, payoffs are $0, $0 and $20. If the premium paid was $7, simple profit at expiry before financing/fees is −$7, −$7 and +$13.

Before expiry, an option price is not simply its payoff at today's share price. Remaining time and possible outcomes matter. Volatility describes dispersion; implied volatility is the model input consistent with an observed option price. A surface supplies inputs at different strikes and maturities. These examples introduce meaning, not a full option-pricing model.

After lesson 17 and the fixed-cash-flow curve example, open swap-repricing.md for the optional two-payment extension. Calculate one floating and fixed payment first, then value both payments. Compare forecast and discount changes only after that baseline reconciles. The later daily-P&L exercise is a separate task and is not needed to start this same-time comparison.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.example:
Swap period: $1m × (5% − 4%) × 0.5 = +$5,000 to the bank
Call expiry payoff at share price $120: max(120 − 100, 0) = $20
Call simple profit after $7 premium: $20 − $7 = $13

exercise.prompt: Try explaining: Can the swap's $1m notional or its next $5,000 payment be used as its total fair value?
exercise.solution: No. The notional sizes payments; the next payment is only one cash flow. Value considers the remaining contract and current inputs.

lessons.title: 9. Translate an input move into money
lessons.takeaway: Background for lesson 17 and lesson 23.

sections.title: Explanation
paragraphs: A sensitivity answers a local "what if" question. Here +$12,000 per basis point means that increasing the specified rate input by 1bp increases value by approximately $12,000. A move of −2bp therefore suggests −$24,000. Other systems use different signs or bump definitions.

Vega measures response to a volatility change. If vega is $5,000 per volatility percentage point, a move from 20% to 21% suggests +$5,000 for positive vega. The change is one volatility point, not a 100% or 1.00-decimal change.

Correlation concerns how variables move together. It can matter for a payoff linked to two shares. It is neither the volatility of one share nor a guarantee of future co-movement. Changing an uncertain correlation and repricing helps investigate significance.

These are local approximations. Large moves, option curvature and interactions can break a simple sensitivity-times-move estimate. Hold other inputs fixed when isolating an effect, then compare with full repricing.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.example:
Rate move: 5.00% → 4.98% = −2bp
Signed sensitivity: +$12,000/bp → approximate change −$24,000
Volatility move: 20% → 21% = +1 vol point
Vega: +$5,000/vol point → approximate change +$5,000

exercise.prompt: Try explaining: Does a volatility move from 20% to 21% equal 1bp?
exercise.solution: No. It is one percentage point, or 100 basis points in percentage arithmetic. Use the stated vega unit rather than reusing a rate sensitivity unit.

lessons.title: 10. Netting and collateral change exposure
lessons.takeaway: Background for lesson 21 and lesson 27.

sections.title: Explanation
paragraphs: Suppose the same counterparty owes the bank $100 on one contract and the bank owes it $80 on another. The arithmetic net is $20. Whether the bank may rely on that net after default depends on enforceable agreements and the applicable method. Matching a customer name in two rows does not establish legal netting.

Collateral is security supporting an obligation. If an eligible $15 collateral amount covers a $20 exposure, the residual in this simplified example is $5. Real exposure calculations also consider timing, eligibility, haircuts, disputes, future changes and agreement terms. Collateral does not erase the original trades.

Keep payment netting, close-out netting, accounting balance-sheet offset and valuation aggregation distinct. Permission for one does not automatically permit the others. These concepts explain why agreement and legal-entity identifiers matter to CVA, funding and risk systems.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.example:
Contract A: bank is owed $100
Contract B: bank owes $80
Arithmetic net: $20, conditional on the relevant netting treatment
Eligible collateral: $15
Simplified current uncovered amount: $5

exercise.prompt: Try explaining: Two trades share a customer ID. Is that enough to net them in a production calculation?
exercise.solution: No. Establish the legal entities, agreement, enforceability and conditions of the particular calculation. Otherwise the apparent $20 may not be the eligible net exposure.

lessons.title: 11. From a balance sheet to a capital ratio
lessons.takeaway: Background for lesson 25 and lesson 29.

sections.title: Explanation
paragraphs: A balance sheet separates assets, liabilities and equity. If a simplified bank has assets of $1,000 and liabilities of $900, accounting equity is $100. Equity is the residual, not a special cash account.

Regulatory capital starts from eligible components and applies prescribed adjustments. Accounting equity is not automatically CET1. Assume, purely for illustration, the bank's capital reconciliation produces CET1 of $80 after all other eligibility rules and adjustments.

Risk-weighted assets (RWA) are a regulatory risk measure used as a denominator. They are not simply the assets shown on the balance sheet. With RWA of $800 and CET1 of $80, the ratio is 10%. A final AVA deduction of $2 gives CET1 of $78 and a ratio of 9.75%, holding everything else fixed.

The deduction reduces the regulatory measure. It is not a $2 cash payment and does not by itself change the accounting fair-value journal. Nor does this single ratio establish the bank's total regulatory compliance.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.example:
Accounting equity: $1,000 − $900 = $100
Assumed eligible CET1 after other adjustments: $80
Before AVA: $80 / $800 = 10.00%
After final $2 AVA: $78 / $800 = 9.75%
Change: −0.25 percentage points = −25bp

exercise.prompt: Try explaining: Does the $2 AVA deduction mean the bank pays $2 cash to someone?
exercise.solution: No. It changes the regulatory capital calculation. Cash, accounting equity and regulatory capital are different measures.

lessons.title: 12. Read a percentile before using it
lessons.takeaway: Background for lesson 26.

sections.title: Explanation
paragraphs: Imagine 100 equally weighted plausible prices sorted from low to high. A low-tail point has most outcomes above it; a high-tail point has most outcomes below it. Percentiles describe location within a specified distribution, not a guaranteed future selling price.

In the continuous normal distribution assumed by the lab, mean minus 1.28155 standard deviations is the 10th percentile. There is 10% model probability below it and 90% above. For a long asset, a lower price is adverse. For a short position, the adverse direction is higher, so the corresponding point is the 90th percentile.

Mean 100 and standard deviation 0.20 give approximately 99.7437 and 100.2563. Doubling standard deviation doubles the distance from the mean. A standard deviation is a measure of spread, not a bid-offer quote or a fixed regulatory haircut.

Real valuation evidence is not automatically a normal distribution. Dependent dealer quotes, sparse observations and stale prices can make a naive statistical calculation misleading. The lab illustrates direction and probability only; calibration, expert judgement and the regulatory method are separate steps.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.example:
Long direction:  10% below | 99.7437 | 90% above
Centre:          100.0000
Short direction: 90% below |100.2563 | 10% above
Assumed standard deviation: 0.20 price points

exercise.prompt: Try explaining: Does a 90% certainty objective mean deducting 10% of every position?
exercise.solution: No. The percentage describes probability under a specified assessment, not the size of a price haircut.

lessons.title: 13. Reconcile a whole day, including cash and FX
lessons.takeaway: Background for lesson 30 and lesson 31.

sections.title: Explanation
paragraphs: Opening quantity 100 plus 20 bought minus 30 sold leaves 90 shares. In the downloadable EUR case, raw carrying value falls from 10,000 to 9,360, but net cash received is 1,160. Raw period economic return is therefore 520, not a loss of 640.

A deduction rising from 20 to 35 reduces the local result by 15 to 505 EUR. Translate each carrying value and cash flow at its supplied rate: opening EURUSD 1.10, closing and event rates 1.12. The reporting-currency result is 765.20 USD.

One explicit attribution convention translates local return at closing FX and separates FX on the opening carrying amount and on cash flows. The bridge is 565.60 + 199.60 + 0 = 765.20 USD. Different attribution order can allocate interactions differently; the total must still reconcile.

The workbook also compares FIFO with weighted-average cost and a two-for-one split. Cost allocation changes the realised/unrealised split, while the stated total economic result is unchanged. A split changes units and per-share price without creating a gain by itself.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.example:
Opening adjusted value EUR 9,980 ×1.10 = USD 10,978
Closing adjusted value EUR 9,325 ×1.12 = USD 10,444
Signed cash EUR 1,160 ×1.12 = USD 1,299.20
Return: 10,444 −10,978 +1,299.20 = USD 765.20

lessons.title: 14. Reprice the same cash flows with different inputs
lessons.takeaway: Background for lesson 17, lesson 18 and lesson 23.

sections.title: Explanation
paragraphs: A fixed two-payment instrument pays EUR 50 in year one and EUR 1,050 in year two. FO discount factors are 0.95 and 0.90; independent factors are 0.94 and 0.88. Multiply each payment by its factor and sum.

FO value is 992.50; independent value 971.00. The −21.50 difference decomposes into −0.50 for year one and −21.00 for year two. This exact input bridge is linear in discount factors. It is not a full swap pricer because the cash flows are fixed.

In a separate flat annual-rate example, changing 5% to 6% gives an exact value change of −18.333927. A derivative-based first-order estimate gives −18.594104: the 0.260178 residual reflects curvature. Rates and discount factors are different input coordinates.

Before selecting a curve, check valuation date, currency, collateral/discounting basis, contractual conventions and source independence. Matching arithmetic is not evidence that the chosen curve is suitable.

exercise.prompt: Try explaining: Why does exact discount-factor attribution reconcile while the rate sensitivity has a residual?

lessons.title: 15. From a trade to a value
lessons.takeaway: A trade describes a contract. A valuation estimates what that contract is worth at a particular time.

sections.title: The concept
paragraphs: Separate notional, price, market value and profit.

Start with a bond: the issuer borrows money, pays coupons and promises principal at maturity. The holder owns those future cash flows. A quoted price of 98.50 usually means 98.50 per 100 of face value. It does not mean the whole position is worth 98.50.

An equity position is different: shares × currency price per share gives market value. A swap exchanges streams of cash flows, such as fixed interest for floating interest. Its notional helps calculate payments; the notional is usually not the swap's market value. An option gives a right, rather than an obligation, and its value depends on the possible future outcomes as well as today's underlying price.

Mark-to-market uses relevant market prices. Mark-to-model calculates value from contractual cash flows and market inputs. A model is not automatically unreliable: a vanilla swap can have a well-supported model value. Equally, a price on a screen is not automatically suitable evidence for your exact position.
Always attach a valuation date, currency, position quantity, product identifier and convention to a number. "Value = 9.85m" without those attributes is an incomplete record.

sections.title: Worked example: One position, four different numbers
sections.example:
Face amount       $10,000,000
Clean price        98.50 per 100
Clean market value $9,850,000
Accrued interest   $40,000
Dirty value        $9,890,000
sections.exampleNote: Divide the per-100 quote by 100 first: 98.50 / 100 = 0.985. Multiply by face amount to get $9,850,000 clean value, then add $40,000 accrued interest once. Clean price excludes that accrued interest; dirty value includes it. The bond lab holds accrued interest fixed to isolate price changes.

sections.title: Go deeper
paragraphs: A position is often an aggregation of several trades. A trade identifier and a security identifier are not interchangeable. One bond can appear in many trades and books. Equity quantity, bond face amount and derivative notional require different valuation functions. Contract features such as settlement date, coupon schedule, optionality and collateral agreement can change the cash flows or discounting.

sections.title: Data & systems
paragraphs: Expected fields: TradeId, InstrumentId, Product, Book, ValuationDate, Currency, SignedQuantity or SignedNotional, PriceConvention, AccruedInterest. Check identifier joins and units before investigating the pricing model.

sections.title: Common trap
paragraphs: A $100m swap notional is not a $100m asset. A change of 0.15 price points on a per-100 quote is 0.15% of face value, not 15%.

lessons.title: 16. What fair value is trying to measure
lessons.takeaway: Fair value asks what market participants would exchange at the measurement date, rather than what you hope the position will earn.

sections.title: The concept
paragraphs: Understand exit value and why a mid price needs context.

Imagine two separate questions: "What did we pay?" and "What is it worth today?" Historical transaction price answers the first. Fair value answers the second using an orderly market-participant exit perspective. It is not a forced fire-sale estimate or a promise of the exact price your next trade will achieve.

A principal market is the market with the greatest volume and activity for the instrument that the entity can access. This matters when screens show different prices on different venues. Valuation uses the relevant market and consistent measurement-time assumptions.

For a simple long position, the bid is what a dealer offers to pay; the ask is what they charge to sell. Mid sits between them. Accounting permits the point within the spread that best represents fair value; bid for assets and ask for liabilities are permitted conventions, not an automatic universal formula. Transaction costs are not part of IFRS 13 fair value.
A valuation method must produce a result consistent with the fair-value objective and supported by the contract and evidence.

sections.title: Worked example: A spread is a range, not two contradictory prices
sections.example:
Dealer bid         99.80
Dealer ask        100.20
Mid               100.00
Long face amount  $10m
Mid-to-bid cost    $20,000
sections.exampleNote: The $20k illustrates the economics of exiting at bid. Whether and how a booked adjustment is required depends on the existing mark and applicable accounting policy.

sections.title: Go deeper
paragraphs: A quoted price for an identical instrument in an active market generally has priority. Holding a large block does not automatically justify an accounting blockage discount to that Level 1 quote. Prudential concentration adjustments answer a different question. Keep the unit of account, the market-participant premise and the purpose of the adjustment separate.

sections.title: Data & systems
paragraphs: Keep PriceSide (bid/mid/ask), CleanDirty, QuoteTime, Market and SettlementDate alongside Price. Two valid prices can look inconsistent because their conventions or timestamps differ.

sections.title: Common trap
paragraphs: Do not subtract bid-offer twice when the front-office value is already on the relevant exit basis. Do not turn every liquidity concern into an accounting discount.

sections.title: Choose the market before measuring the price
paragraphs: Use the accessible principal market even if another venue offers a better price. Without a principal market, select the most advantageous accessible market using net proceeds after transaction and transport costs. Transaction costs then stay outside fair value; location-related transport costs can affect it.

lessons.title: 17. Market data and the model underneath
lessons.takeaway: A model turns a contract and a set of inputs into a value. Changing the input can change the value without changing the contract.

sections.title: The concept
paragraphs: Curves, discount factors, spreads, volatility and sensitivity.

Start with one payment before working with a curve: a supplied discount factor of 0.95 turns a future 100-unit receipt into 95 units of present value. A second receipt of 50 with factor 0.90 contributes 45, giving 140 in total. The factors are supplied inputs here; selecting or constructing a market curve is a separate task.

A discount factor converts a future cash flow to today's value. In a simple annual-compounding example, PV = cash flow / (1 + rate)^years. A curve is a set of rates or discount factors across maturities. Real pricing also needs calendars, day-count conventions, interpolation and settlement rules.

For a fixed-versus-floating swap, think "PV of what I receive minus PV of what I pay." Forecast curves estimate future floating payments; discount curves bring the payments back to today. Collateral and currency affect the appropriate curves. A curve mismatch can therefore produce an IPV difference even when both systems use the same contract.

A credit spread is an additional yield associated with credit and other market effects relative to a reference. Volatility describes the variability used in option pricing; an implied volatility is backed out of traded option prices. A volatility surface varies by strike and maturity. Correlation describes joint movement and can matter greatly for multi-asset products.

Sensitivity connects input differences to currency amounts. DV01 is a rate sensitivity per basis point under a stated sign convention. Vega measures sensitivity to volatility under a stated unit. Exact repricing is the safer reference when nonlinear effects are material.

sections.title: Worked example: A small input gap can mean a large value gap
sections.example:
Signed sensitivity  +$12,000 per bp
Independent − FO    −2 bp
Linear value change −$24,000
sections.exampleNote: This is a first-order estimate, with sensitivity explicitly defined as dV for a +1bp move. Some systems display DV01 using the opposite sign. Always inspect the definition.

sections.title: Go deeper
paragraphs: An input difference is not directly a price difference. For a nonlinear instrument, ΔV is approximately delta × Δx plus one-half gamma × Δx², with cross terms when several inputs move. Sensitivity-based approximations are useful for prioritising exceptions, but replacing the complete input set and repricing avoids assuming all changes are small and independent. For a changed-case calculation, open valuation-transfer.md in the swap-repricing practice files. Predict a 10 bp forward bump before running the test, then fix that rate and explain why the forecast bump stops changing the cash flow.

sections.title: Data & systems
paragraphs: CurveId, Tenor, QuoteUnit, CurveDate, CalibrationVersion, DiscountingAgreement and ModelVersion are part of lineage. A percent/decimal error (5 vs 0.05) can dwarf genuine market movements.

sections.title: Common trap
paragraphs: 1 basis point = 0.01 percentage point = 0.0001 in decimal rate. One volatility point usually means 1 percentage point, but verify the system's vega unit.

lessons.title: 18. IPV: an independent challenge
lessons.takeaway: IPV tests whether prices or model inputs are independently supportable. It is a process, not merely a subtraction.

sections.title: The concept
paragraphs: Follow the full process from population to sign-off.

Independent price verification adds a control separate from the desk that owns the position. Basel guidance distinguishes it from daily marking and calls for independent verification at least monthly, with greater frequency where appropriate. Your bank can impose a more frequent cycle.

Begin by reconciling the population: which positions are in scope, and are any missing? Obtain independent evidence, validate the source, align units and conventions, compare or reprice, investigate differences, then record a conclusion. A control is incomplete if it produces an exception but nobody owns the resolution.

Direct-price IPV compares a usable independent price with the front-office mark. Input IPV compares curves, volatilities or other inputs, often by repricing the same position. Keep market-data differences distinct from model differences: otherwise a model fault can be hidden in a price exception.

A zero difference is evidence only if the comparator is credible. Copying the front-office mark into the independent field produces a perfect match and no independent assurance. Track independence, coverage and evidence quality alongside differences.

sections.example:
Population → source validation → normalisation
→ independent price or revaluation
→ difference → exception investigation
→ approved action → reconciliation → sign-off

paragraphs: Possible outcomes include "verified", "requires investigation", "unverified due to insufficient evidence", "mark corrected", or "adjustment approved". Missing evidence must not become a zero difference. Coverage measures should distinguish verified, proxy-verified, unverified and excluded positions; document why exclusions are legitimate.

sections.title: Data & systems
paragraphs: Keep RunId, PositionSnapshotId, SourceSnapshotId, IndependentPrice, RepricedValue, Difference, EvidenceStatus, ExceptionOwner, Resolution and ApprovalId. Store original observations as well as the selected result.

sections.title: Common trap

quiz.explanation: The fallback hides a coverage failure. Preserve a missing/unverified status and route it for review.

lessons.title: 19. Sources, tolerances and exceptions
lessons.takeaway: A tolerance prioritises investigation; it does not certify that a valuation is correct.

sections.title: The concept
paragraphs: Learn what makes a price usable and a difference actionable.

Source quality is multidimensional: relevance to the instrument, timestamp, executability, size, independence, number of contributors and whether the market is active. A consensus price can be useful, but ten contributors repeating the same stale information are not ten independent observations.

A practical source preference might start with relevant transactions or executable quotes and then use evaluated prices, consensus, proxies or expert judgement. This is not a universal ranking: a current, well-matched evaluated price may be more relevant than a tiny stale transaction.

An exception can arise from a currency impact, a price/input threshold or a data-quality failure. Record each trigger separately. A toy rule in this hub flags a monetary difference over a configurable tolerance; an unreliable source separately produces "unverified". These are learning rules, not industry-wide limits.

Investigate the cause before the accounting action: incorrect position, timestamp mismatch, clean/dirty mismatch, stale source, different curves, real price disagreement or a model problem. Retain both signed impact and absolute magnitude so favourable and adverse differences cannot disappear through netting.

sections.title: Worked example: Same price difference, very different impact
sections.example:
FO 99.80; independent 99.65
Difference = −0.15 price points
$2m long face   → −$3,000
$20m long face  → −$30,000
$20m short face → +$30,000
sections.exampleNote: Signed notional determines the P&L direction. Absolute impact can be useful for triage; it is not the signed adjustment to book.

sections.title: Go deeper
paragraphs: An exception record should answer these questions: what failed, how much is affected, which evidence was used, who investigated, what decision was made and when it expires. Ageing matters: recurring exceptions may reveal a structural coverage gap. Overrides need a reason, an approver and an expiry or review date. A source hierarchy should be versioned so a rerun is explainable.

sections.title: Data & systems
paragraphs: An INNER JOIN against the price feed silently drops unmatched positions. Preserve the position population with a left join, explicit missing flags and row-count/value reconciliation. Deduplicate quotes using source identifiers and timestamps before selecting a price.

sections.title: Common trap
paragraphs: Do not average every quote blindly. A stale quote, a different currency or a different seniority is not an equally plausible observation.

quiz.question: A $30k difference is below an internal $50k threshold, but the independent quote is six weeks stale. What follows?
options: Investigate source quality independently of the amount
Use zero as the independent price
quiz.explanation: Numerical materiality and evidence quality are separate controls. A stale comparator can invalidate the test itself.

lessons.title: 20. Reserves and the accounting value bridge
lessons.takeaway: A valuation adjustment has a reason, a basis, a sign and a scope. "Reserve" alone does not tell you what it does.

sections.title: The concept
paragraphs: Keep mark corrections, reserves and movements separate.

Banks use "reserve" in different ways. Here, an accounting valuation adjustment changes the value recognised in the accounts to reflect the applicable measurement basis. A mark correction fixes an identified wrong mark. A reserve may address uncertainty or an aspect not already captured. Both require a clear basis and must avoid overlap.

For a long asset in our examples, a downward adjustment is shown as a positive deduction: accounting fair value = raw value − deductions. Ledger systems may instead store the adjustment as a signed negative number. For liabilities, cash flows and own-credit effects, a generic "always subtract" rule is unsafe.

Reserve balance and reserve movement are different fields. If a deduction rises from $20k to $35k, the incremental negative valuation effect is $15k, not $35k again. Releasing a deduction can create a positive movement; explain why the underlying need changed.

Accounting presentation can involve P&L or other comprehensive income depending on the instrument and classification. A regulatory AVA belongs to the capital calculation rather than automatically becoming an additional accounting journal.

sections.title: Worked example: A bridge that reconciles
sections.example:
Raw clean value          $10,200,000
Approved price correction  −$100,000
Bid-offer adjustment        −$60,000
Model adjustment            −$40,000
Accounting fair value    $10,000,000
sections.exampleNote: The amounts are synthetic and assumed non-overlapping. An actual book must establish whether the raw mark already includes any of these effects.

sections.title: Go deeper
paragraphs: A reserve engine needs stock, movement and attribution. Opening balance + new positions + market change + methodology change + FX translation + releases + other approved effects should reconcile to closing balance under defined sign conventions. Attribution is often approximate when inputs interact; a residual should be visible rather than silently forced to zero.

sections.title: Data & systems
paragraphs: AdjustmentId, Type, ScopeKey, CalculationBasis, Currency, SignedAmount, EffectiveDate, Reason, ModelVersion and ApprovalId make the bridge auditable. Keep position-level allocations separate from the original portfolio-level calculation.

sections.title: Common trap
paragraphs: A portfolio reserve allocation is not necessarily a stand-alone reserve calculation for each trade. Summing allocated and original portfolio amounts double counts.

quiz.question: A long-asset reserve deduction increases from $20k to $35k. With all else unchanged, the valuation movement is…
quiz.explanation: The balance changed by $15k. The increased deduction reduces value by that amount.

lessons.title: 21. Bid-offer, liquidity and model uncertainty
lessons.takeaway: Name the uncertainty before calculating an adjustment. Similar-looking deductions can measure different things.

sections.title: The concept
paragraphs: Distinguish the reasons behind adjustments.

Bid-offer captures the difference between a reference mark and an appropriate exit basis. Liquidity concerns include the availability and depth of trading. Concentration adds the issue of position size relative to market capacity. These can interact, so separate labels alone do not prove that adjustments are independent.

Model uncertainty arises when plausible modelling choices produce different values. A programming defect is different: a known implementation error should be corrected and its effects assessed. Reserving for a known defect without fixing it is not a durable control.

CVA reflects counterparty credit effects in derivative valuation; DVA reflects own-credit effects. Funding valuation adjustments address relevant funding economics under the methodology used. Their calculation can depend on netting, collateral, future exposure and funding assumptions. They are not simply fixed percentages of notional.

A valuation adjustment is not the same as a capital requirement for the risk of its future movement. In particular, a CVA amount and a regulatory CVA risk capital charge answer different questions. Also distinguish loan-loss allowances from the fair-value reserves studied here.

sections.title: Worked example: Ask a different question for each line
sections.example:
Bid-offer: What exit side is appropriate?
Model: Which plausible valuation is defensible?
Concentration: How long and how costly to unwind?
Credit: What does non-performance do to value?
sections.exampleNote: Use the questions as a map. You still need the applicable policy, unit of account and evidence before recording an amount.

sections.title: Go deeper
paragraphs: A model comparison should hold other conditions constant if the goal is isolating model uncertainty. Repricing with a different model and a different market snapshot mixes two effects. For options, interpolation and extrapolation can matter even when the headline volatility input looks identical. For portfolios, netting may alter close-out or credit calculations; never infer netting eligibility from a shared customer name.

sections.title: Data & systems
paragraphs: NettingSetId, CollateralAgreementId and LegalEntity may be essential calculation keys. A broken mapping can affect CVA/FVA or close-out results even if all trade prices look correct.

sections.title: Common trap
paragraphs: Do not apply a blanket accounting concentration discount to an unadjusted Level 1 price. Prudential concentration assessment is a separate exercise.

quiz.explanation: Known errors are not simply alternative defensible model assumptions. Fix the defect and assess affected valuations.

lessons.title: 22. Level 1, Level 2, Level 3
lessons.takeaway: Fair Value Hierarchy classifies the measurement by the significance and observability of its inputs, not by product name or code complexity.

sections.title: The concept
paragraphs: Classify the evidence supporting the valuation.

Level 1 uses unadjusted quoted prices for identical instruments in active markets. Level 2 uses observable inputs other than qualifying Level 1 prices. Level 3 involves an unobservable input significant to the overall measurement. When inputs span levels, the lowest significant input level determines the overall classification.

An exchange-traded share with a qualifying unadjusted quote is a natural Level 1 example. A vanilla swap valued from observable curves is a common Level 2 example. A structured derivative whose value materially depends on unobservable long-term correlation can be Level 3.

These are conditional examples, not product lookup rules. An exchange listing does not by itself demonstrate an active market. A vendor-provided price is not automatically Level 2. A sophisticated model can still use observable inputs, and a simple instrument can depend on a significant unobservable input.
Classification helps explain how the number was obtained. It is not a direct credit rating, liquidity score, probability of loss or rule for how much AVA to calculate.

sections.title: Worked example: One important input can change the classification
sections.example:
Discount curve       observable
FX forwards          observable
Long-term correlation unobservable
Correlation significant to total value? Yes
Illustrative outcome: Level 3
sections.exampleNote: Counting observable inputs misses the point. Ninety-nine observable inputs do not cancel one significant unobservable input.

sections.title: Go deeper
paragraphs: Review the measurement as a whole. A significant adjustment to an observable input can change the hierarchy outcome when it introduces unobservable assumptions. Record the assessment as of the reporting date, including the evidence supporting market activity and input availability. Transfers between levels need reasons and the relevant reporting policy.

sections.title: Data & systems
paragraphs: Keep InputObservability separate from OverallFVLevel. Store SignificanceAssessment, EvidenceDate and ClassificationReason. A single vendor flag rarely supplies the whole classification rationale.

sections.title: Common trap
paragraphs: FVH is not calculated by averaging levels: Level 1 + Level 3 does not give Level 2.

quiz.question: A complex swap model uses only relevant observable significant inputs, without a qualifying Level 1 quote. Its likely level is…
options: Level 3 because the code is complex
quiz.explanation: The evidence and input significance determine the hierarchy, not the length of the model code.

lessons.title: 23. Observability and significance in practice
lessons.takeaway: "Unobservable" describes the evidence. "Significant" describes the effect on the whole measurement. You need both.

sections.title: The concept
paragraphs: Move from a flag to a defensible assessment.

An input may be well supported at a five-year tenor and weakly supported at twenty years. Extrapolating a curve beyond available market evidence introduces assumptions even when the earlier curve points are observable. A price source name cannot resolve this alone.

One way to understand significance is to change the uncertain input across a defensible range and examine the effect on the complete value. That does not create a universal numerical threshold. Banks establish assessment methods and governance, and qualitative factors can matter.

For technology work, distinguish missing data from an approved unobservable estimate. Missing is a data/control state; an estimated input can be an intentional methodological choice with documentation. Treating null as zero collapses that distinction.

Classification can change when markets become inactive, a significant input loses observable support, or new evidence becomes available. A transfer is not necessarily a trade event. It can be an evidence event.

sections.title: Worked example: A useful sensitivity question
sections.example:
Base structured-note value  $2.00m
Value at low correlation    $1.72m
Value at high correlation   $2.21m
Evidence for correlation    internal estimate
sections.exampleNote: The range suggests that correlation deserves a serious significance assessment. It does not prove a universal percentage cut-off for Level 3.

sections.title: Go deeper
paragraphs: Document the alternative inputs, why the range is plausible, how the valuation was rerun, the measure used to assess significance and who approved the conclusion. Near-zero net values can make percentage tests misleading: a $10k change relative to a $1k net value is huge, even though the gross cash-flow legs may be much larger. Avoid invented automatic thresholds.

sections.title: Data & systems
paragraphs: Store observability by input, tenor and valuation date. Version overrides and reference the evidence. A portfolio-level "Level 2" flag copied from the previous month can conceal a newly significant unobservable input.

sections.title: Common trap
paragraphs: "Quoted by a broker" and "observable for this valuation" are not synonyms. Relevance and support matter.

quiz.explanation: The overall hierarchy follows the lowest significant input level, not every immaterial input.

lessons.title: 24. FVH classification and reporting exercises
lessons.takeaway: A useful classification record explains the decision and its evidence, rather than storing only "2" or "3".

sections.title: The concept
paragraphs: Explain the level, the evidence and what could change it.

Consider a bond valued using comparable bonds and an observable issuer spread. If the significant inputs are observable and there is no qualifying identical active-market quote, Level 2 can be appropriate. If an important spread must instead be estimated without market support, the outcome may change.

Consider an illiquid listed share. The word "listed" is not enough to establish Level 1. Investigate market activity and how the value is actually measured. Conversely, a Level 3 position is not automatically mispriced: its valuation relies on significant judgement that must be explained.

Reporting usually requires reconciling the hierarchy population to accounting fair values, with consistent currency conversion and scope. A total of trade notionals is not a fair-value disclosure total. Netting and presentation must follow the relevant reporting rules.
Explain the proposed level, its supporting evidence and a fact that would change the classification.

sections.title: Worked example: Explain a classification in one sentence
sections.example:
"Level 3 because the unobservable long-term
volatility assumption materially affects the
overall measurement; review approved under
evidence pack EV-102."
sections.exampleNote: This is much more useful than "Level 3 because exotic". It connects an input, a valuation effect and a controlled decision.

sections.title: Go deeper
paragraphs: Do not confuse an FVH transfer with a reserve movement. Both may be caused by deteriorating evidence, but one changes a classification and the other changes a measured amount. A classification change can happen with no immediate value change. Keep the two event types distinct in reporting and movement explanations.

sections.title: Data & systems
paragraphs: Reconcile sum of accounting FV by currency/entity and level against the defined accounting population. Investigate unmapped levels, duplicate classifications, out-of-period overrides and stale evidence. Preserve the timing policy for transfers.

sections.title: Common trap
paragraphs: If the system assigns Level 3 only when reserve > 0, it is encoding the wrong relationship. Observability and adjustment amount are separate dimensions.

sections.title: From Level 3 classification to a reporting record
paragraphs: Recurring Level 3 reporting reconciles opening and closing balances. Disclose movements separately, transfer reasons/timing policy, P&L lines and unrealised P&L for holdings remaining at period-end. Also explain techniques, significant unobservable inputs and valuation processes. Sensitivity disclosures depend on the measurement and significance conditions in paragraph 93(h).

Synthetic asset class, €m:
Opening 100 + purchases 20 − sales 12 − settlements 5 + issues 0 + P&L gains 4 + OCI 0 + transfers in 8 − transfers out 3 = closing 112.
Disclosure record: discounted cash flow; unobservable credit spread 450bp; reasonably possible range 400–500bp; revalued totals 115–109. Explain assumptions, input relationships, transfer reasons and the applicable significance assessment.

lessons.title: 25. PruVal, AVAs and capital
lessons.takeaway: Prudent valuation addresses uncertainty for regulatory capital. An AVA is additional to the relevant uncertainty already recognised in accounting value.

sections.title: The concept
paragraphs: Separate the accounting number from the prudential overlay.

Accounting and prudential measurement serve different purposes. In the EU framework, prudent valuation applies to relevant fair-valued positions in both trading and non-trading books. AVAs reduce Common Equity Tier 1 capital under the CRR. They do not simply overwrite the accounting fair value.

CET1 is a core regulatory capital measure with prescribed inclusions and deductions. It is not cash sitting in a separate account. If CET1 decreases while risk-weighted assets stay fixed, the CET1 ratio decreases. A valuation change and a capital-ratio change are therefore related but different outputs.

Begin conceptually with raw value, identify accounting adjustments already captured and assess the remaining prudential uncertainty. Offset only an adjustment demonstrably addressing the same uncertainty at the appropriate calculation level. Never use an unrelated reserve as a general credit against every AVA.

The general concepts are useful across jurisdictions. The thresholds, implementation details, reporting forms and effective dates must come from the regime and entity that actually apply to your bank.

sections.title: Worked example: Keep the starting points straight
sections.example:
Unadjusted asset value     €10.2m
Same-source accounting adj  €0.2m
Accounting fair value      €10.0m
Total prudent deduction     €0.5m
Incremental deduction       €0.3m
sections.exampleNote: The €0.3m is a schematic residual before any applicable aggregation. Starting from the already-adjusted €10.0m and deducting €0.5m again would double count €0.2m.

sections.title: Go deeper
paragraphs: The teaching bridge uses a long asset and positive deduction magnitudes. Production AVA methodologies can operate on valuation exposures or portfolios with hedges and permitted aggregation. Do not apply the bridge independently to every trade and assume summing those outputs reproduces the regulatory total.

sections.title: Data & systems
paragraphs: AccountingFV, RecognisedSameSourceAdjustment, GrossPrudentRequirement, AVABeforeAggregation and AggregatedAVA are distinct concepts. The mapping needs policy version, jurisdiction, reporting date and calculation scope.

sections.title: Common trap

quiz.explanation: €500k − €200k = €300k, floored at zero. This is before the applicable aggregation methodology.

lessons.title: 26. Market price uncertainty
lessons.takeaway: MPU concerns uncertainty around today's valuation inputs or price, rather than a forecast of tomorrow's market loss.

sections.title: The concept
paragraphs: Separate uncertainty about the mark from market risk tomorrow.

Several credible sources can disagree even at the same time. That spread of evidence suggests uncertainty about the current mark. Before interpreting it, align instrument, side, size, currency, time and convention, and assess dependence between sources.

The EU core framework uses a 90% certainty objective for the prudent point in the plausible range: price or better. For a long asset, the adverse direction is lower; for a liability or a short, it reverses. It is not a rule to take the 90th percentile of prices in every case.

The uncertainty lab uses an explicitly assumed normal distribution and a one-sided 1.28155 standard-deviation multiplier. It is a mathematical teaching device for direction and spread. A handful of dealer quotes does not establish a valid statistical distribution or regulatory calibration.

Data-poor situations need governed expert judgement rather than false precision. Document why the range is plausible, which positions it represents, how sensitivities translate it into value and what evidence could improve the estimate.

sections.title: Worked example: Direction matters
sections.example:
Assumed central price       100.00
Assumed standard deviation    0.20
Toy lower 10th percentile    99.7437
Toy upper 90th percentile   100.2563
sections.exampleNote: Under this invented normal model, 90% of the price distribution lies above the lower point. That illustrates a long-asset adverse direction; it does not prove a real-world 90% exit guarantee.

sections.title: Go deeper
paragraphs: Market risk usually studies changes over a future horizon. Valuation uncertainty asks what price or input is supportable now. The two can interact in stressed markets, but a VaR/expected-shortfall number is not a substitute for an MPU AVA. Netting valuation exposures requires methodological support; opposing notionals alone do not prove the same uncertain input is hedged.

sections.title: Data & systems
paragraphs: SourceRange, DataQuality, InputUncertainty, ValuationExposure, HedgeMapping, ExpertOverlay and CalibrationVersion should be traceable. Preserve rejected source observations and reasons so the selected range can be challenged.

sections.title: Common trap
paragraphs: The 90% target is not a universal 10% haircut, and an observed minimum from five quotes is not automatically the required quantile.

sections.title: Related foundations
paragraphs: Need the background first? Read lesson 12 (Read a percentile before using it).

sections.title: When the ordinary core calculation cannot be performed
paragraphs: A missing feed first creates an evidence problem to investigate. It does not by itself prove that Articles 9–17 are impossible to apply: a permitted, documented expert-based method may still be available. Record the failed method, affected instruments and escalation decision.

If Articles 9–17 cannot be applied to certain positions, Article 7(2)(b) prescribes a fallback: include 100% of net unrealised profit on the related instruments, plus 10% of derivative notional, plus 25% of |fair value − unrealised profit| for non-derivatives. Unrealised profit is the positive fair-value change since inception, using first-in-first-out. The last two terms apply to their respective instrument types. This fallback is distinct from the simplified 0.1% approach.
sections.example:
Synthetic non-derivative, full CET1 impact: inception value €100k; current FV €108k; positive unrealised profit €8k. Fallback = €8k + 25% × |€108k − €8k| = €33k.
Separate derivative: €2m notional, €10k qualifying unrealised profit → €10k + 10%×€2m = €210k. Neither example is a routine haircut for an otherwise calculable position.

lessons.title: 27. Close-out cost and concentration
lessons.takeaway: A mid-price estimate and the cost of exiting a position answer different questions.

sections.title: The concept
paragraphs: Connect spread, size and time to exit.

Close-out cost captures costs associated with the bid-offer spread in the relevant valuation exposure. In the EU core framework, the prudent spread assessment uses the certainty objective and normally applies half the assessed full spread, with recognition of applicable existing adjustments. Do not subtract the full bid-to-ask spread from a long position already at mid.

Concentration concerns positions that may require an extended period to exit. Market capacity, position size, uncertainty during the exit period and an exit strategy can matter. It is not enough to divide notional by daily volume and call the result an AVA.

Hedged risks can have different close-out behaviour from standalone positions. You need a defined valuation exposure and justified netting or offset assumptions. The actual cost of unwinding a portfolio is not always the sum of costs of closing each trade independently.

The relationship with accounting adjustments must be explicit. An accounting bid-offer reserve can already cover part of the same uncertainty. A separate model reserve cannot automatically offset close-out cost.

sections.title: Go deeper

Treat a participation-rate calculation as an operational scenario, not a prescribed regulatory formula. Accounting restrictions on blockage factors must remain separate from prudential concentration rules.

lessons.title: 28. Model risk and the other AVA categories
lessons.takeaway: Nine category names form a coverage map. They do not mean nine independent percentages should be added to every trade.

sections.title: The concept
paragraphs: Know all nine categories and their overlaps.

Model risk examines uncertainty from defensible alternative models or calibrations. In the EU framework, market-derived input uncertainty already addressed by MPU is excluded from model-risk treatment to avoid overlap. A review should distinguish uncertain assumptions from known defects.

Unearned credit spreads and investing/funding costs address valuation uncertainty in credit and funding adjustments. Their uncertainty is allocated through market price uncertainty, close-out cost and model risk under the EU RTS. They are not extra duplicate buckets to stack on top of those same amounts.

Concentrated positions address the challenge of exiting size. Future administrative costs concern relevant future servicing/administration under the regulatory conditions. Early termination concerns the effect of non-contractual termination behaviour. Operational-risk AVA addresses valuation-process operational uncertainty under the specified approach.

Applicability and prescribed treatment matter. You cannot assume each category is material for each product, or that a zero result means no assessment is required. The sources panel provides the legal articles for deeper study.

3 Model risk                  4 Unearned credit spreads
5 Investing / funding costs   6 Concentrated positions

sections.exampleNote: Articles 9–17 of EU 2016/101 cover these areas. Categories 4 and 5 feed the uncertainty categories under their specified treatment; avoid duplicate totals.

sections.title: Go deeper
paragraphs: For an illustrative model-risk discussion, hold trade data and market snapshot fixed: Model A values a long asset at 12.4m and Model B at 11.8m. The 0.6m difference identifies a question; it is not automatically the correct reserve or AVA. Assess model validity, plausible alternatives, the selected prudent point, what is already booked and the permitted aggregation. Article 17 of the referenced EU RTS still mentions an Advanced Measurement Approach (AMA) zero condition and otherwise prescribes 10% of aggregated MPU plus close-out cost AVAs. CRR3 has since removed AMA for operational-risk capital. Do not treat that old zero condition as a current general option; check the current supervisory interpretation. EBA question 2025_7506 was rejected without a substantive answer, so it does not resolve the mismatch.

sections.title: Data & systems
paragraphs: Use an uncertainty taxonomy and overlap mapping. Record a gross uncertainty assessment separately from the final reporting bucket. A data model with nine unrelated columns can obscure required allocation and reconciliation.

sections.title: Common trap
paragraphs: CVA is not the same as unearned-credit-spread AVA. One is a valuation component; the other addresses prudential uncertainty around relevant valuation components.

quiz.explanation: The RTS prescribes how these uncertainties feed other categories. A naive sum can count the same uncertainty twice.

lessons.title: 29. Approaches, aggregation and CET1
lessons.takeaway: Scope and aggregation are part of the methodology. A correct trade formula can still produce the wrong regulatory total.

sections.title: The concept
paragraphs: Understand the regulatory machinery without mistaking it for a toy calculator.

Under the referenced EU RTS, an eligible simplified approach uses 0.1% of the defined aggregate absolute fair-valued asset and liability amount, with a €15bn threshold and specific eligibility/scope rules. It is not 0.1% of derivative notional. Individual and consolidated eligibility both matter.

The core approach calculates valuation uncertainty by category with prescribed aggregation. Only permitted offsets and diversification belong in that calculation. The first three categories have Annex methods; do not apply a generic "halve the total AVA" instruction to all nine categories.

Read the symbols before substituting numbers. In this Annex discussion, PV means prudent value, not the present value used in lesson 17. FV is the method-defined fair-value baseline, EV is expected value, and alpha is an aggregation factor. The worked Annex extension below defines the calculation scope and gives both methods using one supplied exposure.

For Annex Method 1, APVA = (1 − alpha) × (FV − PV), using the method's definitions and required prior treatment. Alpha is 50% in the referenced post-2020 baseline. Method 2 also uses an expected value: max[0, FV − alpha × EV − (1 − alpha) × PV]. These are method-specific aggregation expressions, not universal trade-level bridge formulas.

The UK has separate rules; its simplified threshold is £13bn in the referenced instrument. As of this edition, the PRA's January 2026 restatement has relevant provisions effective from January 2027. Keep publication date, effective date and reporting date distinct.

sections.title: Worked example: Translate an AVA into a ratio effect

Final AVA deduction       €3m
CET1 after AVA          €997m
Risk-weighted assets  €10,000m
Ratio before / after  10.00% / 9.97%
sections.exampleNote: This holds every other capital item and RWA fixed. The 0.03 percentage-point change equals 3 basis points of capital ratio, not a 3% drop in the ratio.

sections.title: Go deeper
paragraphs: The referenced EU calculation is at least quarterly. A bank may run internal estimates more often. Exactly matching offsets, partial CET1 effects and consolidation rules make the eligible base more nuanced than a gross ledger total. Consultation proposals do not amend production rules until adopted and effective. The app stops before regulatory aggregation. Consult the source for the full conditions.

paragraphs: Regime, RuleVersion, EffectiveFrom, ReportingDate, ConsolidationScope, CET1ImpactProportion, AggregationMethod and Category need controlled definitions. Aggregate currencies only after an approved translation process; do not sum EUR and USD amounts as if they were the same unit.

sections.title: Annex aggregation: decode every symbol
paragraphs: These formulas concern MPU, close-out and model-risk categories. FV is exposure-level fair value after identifiable same-source accounting adjustments. PV here means prudent value, not present value. EV is the expected value across possible exposure values. Alpha is the aggregation factor; the referenced Annex sets it to 50% after 2020. APVA is the exposure amount after aggregation treatment; sum APVAs within the category to obtain its AVA.

Method 1: APVA = (1 − alpha) × (FV − PV). Method 2: APVA = max(0, FV − alpha × EV − (1 − alpha) × PV). Keep consistent exposure, currency and uncertainty source. Never subtract the same booked adjustment again.
sections.example:
Synthetic long-asset exposure, €k, same uncertainty source:
Raw value 1,000; eligible booked deduction 2 → FV 998. Supplied PV 990; EV 996; alpha 0.50.
Method 1: 0.50 × (998 − 990) = 4.
Method 2: max(0, 998 − 0.50×996 − 0.50×990) = 5.
These are alternative calculations, not amounts to add together.

sections.title: Keep the aggregation sequence visible
paragraphs: First define the valuation exposure and calculate its prudent value under the relevant category method. Map only accounting adjustments that address that same uncertainty at the required calculation level. An unrelated reserve cannot reduce this result. Respect the CET1-impact proportion and non-negative AVA requirements.

Next calculate the eligible exposure amounts, apply that category's prescribed aggregation, and combine category results. Credit-spread and investing/funding uncertainty feed the MPU, close-out and model-risk categories as required; do not add them twice. Categories outside the Annex do not receive an automatic 50% discount. A supplied prudent value or expected value is an assumption in these teaching examples, not something the formula itself estimates.

Teaching flow: evidence → exposure/prudent value → eligible same-source booked adjustment → exposure AVA → prescribed category aggregation → category totals → total AVA → CET1 deduction.
If two Method-1 exposures produce APVAs of €4k and €3k, their category AVA is €7k. That is still not the bank's all-category total.

sections.title: Simplified approach: eligibility, matching and breach timeline
paragraphs: The referenced EU threshold is strictly below €15bn. Exactly €15bn fails the condition. Exclude exactly matching offsetting fair-valued assets and liabilities; include other values only in proportion to how valuation changes affect CET1. This is not permission to net all longs against all shorts.

Test both the individual institution and consolidated group. A consolidated breach requires the core approach throughout the consolidation. After two consecutive quarters failing the condition, an institution using the simplified approach must immediately notify its competent authority and agree a plan to implement the core approach within the following two quarters.

Separate timeline: Q1 €15bn and Q2 €15.2bn → notify immediately after Q2 and agree transition within Q3–Q4. Do not wait until Q4 to raise the issue.

lessons.title: 30. Day-one P&L and valuation movements
lessons.takeaway: A model can imply a gain on day one without proving that the gain is immediately recognisable in the accounts.

sections.title: The concept
paragraphs: Understand why a model gain may not be recognised immediately.

Suppose the bank pays 100 to acquire an asset its model values at 103. From the bank's perspective, the apparent 3-unit gain invites a question: does observable market evidence support the difference, or is it created by assumptions that cannot be independently substantiated?

IFRS 9 distinguishes differences evidenced by qualifying quoted prices or a valuation using only observable market data from other differences. In the latter case, the difference is deferred under the prescribed conditions, with later recognition linked to relevant changes including time. This is more specific than "every Level 3 trade has a day-one reserve".

For the opposite perspective, a bank issuing a liability with fair value 103 for cash proceeds 100 has an apparent 3-unit loss, not a gain. Issuing a liability with fair value 100 for proceeds 103 gives an apparent gain of 3. Identify the bank's asset or liability and cash direction before applying the recognition or deferral test.

After day one, explain valuation changes through market movements, new trades, maturities, cash flows, FX, model changes and adjustment movements. A value decrease is not necessarily a loss on its own if a coupon or settlement cash flow was paid during the period.

For systems work, a deferred difference needs a lifecycle: original amount, remaining balance, recognition events and supporting evidence. A fixed amortisation schedule should not be invented merely because it is easy to implement.

sections.exampleNote: $1,005,000 − $1,010,000 + $8,000 = $3,000, before other trades, expenses or FX. Ignoring the coupon would suggest a misleading $5,000 loss.

sections.title: Go deeper
paragraphs: A reserve release, a day-one deferral release and an IPV correction can all affect reported movements but have different causes. Keep them separate in attribution. A method change may produce a one-off movement; compare the same population under old and new methods to isolate it from market and trade changes.

lessons.title: 31. Data lineage, controls and debugging
lessons.takeaway: A reliable valuation result must be reproducible from a defined position snapshot, evidence snapshot, methodology and approved decisions.

sections.title: The concept
paragraphs: Trace a number from market feed to report.

Imagine a user says: "MPU doubled overnight." Start by asking whether the population, inputs, method, offsets, currency conversion or reporting mapping changed. Re-running the latest data does not reproduce yesterday's result if the source snapshots have been overwritten.

Build a chain from trade capture to positions, normalised market data, model valuation, independent comparison, exceptions, accounting adjustments, hierarchy assessment, prudential assessment and reporting. Some steps branch rather than occur strictly in series: FVH classifies the measurement, and model governance supports the whole chain.

Useful controls include completeness reconciliations, duplicate detection, valid units, stale-data checks, sign checks, source independence, mapping coverage and bridge reconciliation. Technical job success means the program ran; it does not mean the population or the valuation is correct.

Make reruns idempotent: the same inputs and version should produce the same logical results without duplicate postings. Late data should trigger a controlled revised run, with an explanation of what changed, rather than silently altering a signed-off report.

sections.title: Worked example: Debug from the outside in
sections.example:
1 Compare run metadata and row counts
2 Reconcile notionals and values by book/currency
3 Compare changed source observations
4 Inspect method and override versions
5 Reprice a representative exception
6 Reconcile results to the report
sections.exampleNote: This order can distinguish a population problem from a valuation problem before you spend hours inside the pricing function.

sections.title: Go deeper
paragraphs: Use stable business keys plus run identifiers. Many-to-many joins can multiply a position when there are several quotes or classifications per instrument. Reduce each source to the intended as-of record before joining, or explicitly retain the one-to-many evidence relation. Money calculations need controlled decimal precision and documented rounding; the browser's floating-point labs are educational, not ledger engines. A zero aggregate difference can conceal different errors: duplicating a 100-unit position and dropping another 100-unit position preserves both total value and row count. Reconcile identifiers and multiplicity as well as amounts. Change one identifier in a copied synthetic fixture and locate the mismatch before recalculating totals.

sections.title: Data & systems
paragraphs: Recommended lineage keys: RunId, PositionSnapshotId, SourceSnapshotId, InstrumentId, ValuationDate, MethodVersion, OverrideId, ApprovalId and ReportingBatchId. Include each source timestamp and its time zone. A local date alone is insufficient.

sections.title: Common trap
paragraphs: An unmatched row that disappears can improve your apparent exception rate. Reconcile the population size as well as the exception count.

sections.title: Make a rule traceable and maintainable
paragraphs: A source record should identify the issuer, jurisdiction, document title, exact article or paragraph, edition/effective date, checked date, access result and change trigger. A calculation record should reference that rule version. The day a PDF was downloaded is not its effective date.

For this edition, the detailed IFRS 13 PDF requires sign-in. The stable IFRS standard page remains a useful entry point; the AASB December 2022 compilation supplies accessible IFRS-aligned paragraphs, excluding Australian-specific provisions. EU source checks used official indexed text where direct access was blocked. This records evidence limits without treating a blocked link as a change in law.

A future amendment, reporting-date change or regulator clarification should trigger a review of affected lessons, formulas and fixtures together. Keep historical reviews immutable and add a new review record. Label proposals separately from enacted requirements.

lessons.title: 32. Put it all together at month-end
lessons.takeaway: You understand the workflow when you can explain the value, the evidence, the adjustments, the hierarchy and the capital effect separately.

sections.title: The concept
paragraphs: Explain a full position without mixing the outputs.

Take the long bond in the month-end case. Its FO clean price is 99.80, the selected independent clean mid is 99.65 and face amount is $20m. The signed IPV difference is −$30k. In the case, an investigation concludes that the FO mark should be corrected. That conclusion is a supplied scenario fact, not something the subtraction alone proves.

After correction, the clean value is $19.93m. An approved $10k bid-offer deduction gives accounting clean fair value of $19.92m. Add $40k fixed accrued interest for the case's accounting dirty value of $19.96m. The case classifies the measurement as Level 2 because the assumed significant inputs are observable and there is no qualifying Level 1 quote.

A supplied gross prudent close-out requirement of $16k with a $10k same-source booked deduction leaves $6k incremental close-out assessment before aggregation. A separate supplied $8k MPU requirement has no same-source booked offset in this scenario. The diagnostic pre-aggregation total is $14k; it is not a final regulatory AVA.

Now explain what would change each result: a different position size changes currency impact, a stale quote changes evidence status, a significant unobservable input can change hierarchy, and an eligible booked adjustment can change the incremental prudential amount. Try a changed case before reopening the worked example: halve the face amount to $10m while holding the two per-100 prices fixed, and halve accrued interest to $20k. Recalculate the signed price difference. Do not automatically halve the separate $10k deduction or the supplied prudential amounts; their revised scope and assumptions would need to be stated. This separates a linear price calculation from unrelated supplied adjustments.

sections.title: Worked example: Five outputs, five questions
sections.example:
IPV difference   −$30k → Does the mark agree?
Accounting FV   $19.96m → What is booked, dirty?
Hierarchy       Level 2 → What evidence supports it?
Pre-agg MPU       $8k → What uncertainty remains?
Pre-agg COC       $6k → What exit uncertainty remains?
sections.exampleNote: Use the full case to reveal each step, inspect the sample data and practise explaining the result without seeing the answer first.

sections.title: Go deeper
paragraphs: A strong work explanation names the baseline, signs, units and calculation level. It says which amounts are scenario assumptions and which are calculated. It also explains unresolved evidence. "The result is $14k" is incomplete without "diagnostic pre-aggregation, not final AVA, USD, this valuation exposure, these same-source offsets".

sections.title: Data & systems
paragraphs: The supplied CSV includes a clean/dirty convention, price evidence, signed quantity and scenario assumptions. Rows intentionally include a stale source, missing source and short position. Treat missing inputs as missing; do not coerce them to zero.

sections.title: Common trap
paragraphs: The $30k price correction fixes the central mark in this case. It is not automatically an eligible offset against the separate residual MPU assessment.

quiz.question: Can the case's $14k pre-aggregation total be reported as the final regulatory AVA without further methodology?
options: No, applicable scope and aggregation still matter
Yes, because the bond is Level 2
quiz.explanation: Correct arithmetic is necessary but the regulatory method also specifies scope, eligibility, offsets and aggregation.
